brief_bullets: Microsoft is phasing out its agreement to rent artificial intelligence computing capacity from Oracle, marking a significant shift in the tech giant's infrastructure strategy. According to reports, Microsoft opted not to renew the contract as the rented capacity no longer aligned with its evolving technical requirements and internal scaling goals. This decision follows a broader reassessment of Microsoft’s multi-billion dollar cloud partnerships as the company prioritizes proprietary hardware and internal data center expansion to support its AI ambitions. While Oracle shares dipped nearly 3% following the news, Microsoft’s stock remained stable, reflecting a strategic pivot toward self-sufficiency in the highly competitive cloud computing market as demand for specialized AI infrastructure continues to accelerate rapidly across the industry.
why_it_matters_bullets: This shift signals Microsoft's move toward infrastructure independence, potentially disrupting Oracle's revenue growth and cloud market positioning.

stories.primary_headline: TCS Nashik case: AIMIM leader Imtiyaz Jaleel named as accused in supplementary chargesheet

primary_source.headline: TCS Nashik case: AIMIM leader Imtiyaz Jaleel named as accused in supplementary chargesheet
primary_source.content: Nashik: All India Majlis-e-Ittehadul Muslimeen (AIMIM) leader Imtiyaz Jaleel has been named an accused by police in a supplementary chargesheet, filed in the sexual harassment and religious conversion case at TCS's Nashik unit, for allegedly helping a key accused when she was absconding.The supplementary chargesheet was filed in the court of Additional Sessions Judge Amit Kharkar in Nashik on Friday, a lawyer representing one of the victims said.Jaleel, a former Lok Sabha MP from Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar (formerly Aurangabad), is accused of helping Nida Khan, a former employee at the TCS Nashik unit and a key accused in the case, when she was absconding.The Nashik police Special Investigation Team (SIT) probing the case at Tata Consultancy Services (TCS) Nashik unit had found connection of Jaleel with AIMIM corporator Mateen Patel, who had been arrested earlier for giving shelter to Nida during her stay in Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar.Accordingly, a notice under section 35 (3) of the Bharatiya Nagrik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS) was served to Jaleel around a month ago, seeking his appearance. The AIMIM Maharashtra unit president subsequently appeared for questioning before the SIT.Now, the SIT has named Jaleel an accused in the chargesheet related to the case registered at the Deolali Camp police station, said the lawyer.Jaleel did not appear in the court and further proceedings will take place as per legal procedures. The court will issue a summons and Jaleel will have to appear before it or apply for bail.TCS sexual harassment case: Five accused given bail by Nashik courtAs per the SIT, Nida was harboured by Patel, the AIMIM corporator from Naregao in Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar, around 200km away from Nashik, in central Maharashtra when police were searching for her. Patel was questioned and arrested on August 8.A case was registered against Patel as well as co-accused Hanif Khan, owner of the flat where Nida was living.The first TCS case was registered at the Deolali Camp police station on March 26. On May 2, a local court rejected her bail application. Khan was arrested from Naregao on May 7 and the court granted her bail on July 6.The SIT is probing a total of nine cases registered in connection with the alleged exploitation, attempt of forceful conversion, hurting religious sentiments, molestation and mental harassment of female employees at the TCS unit.Eight cases were filed at the Mumbai Naka police station in Nashik and one at the Deolali Camp police station. Eight victims came forward with their complaints, and according to police, these incidents were taking place at the unit since July 2022.Nida's specific role, according to the investigation, involved brainwashing one of the victims by giving her a burqa and religious literature.The SIT had earlier filed two chargesheets in the case, in which nearly a dozen people have been named accused so far.After the case came to light, TCS maintained it has adopted a zero-tolerance policy towards harassment and coercion of any form at workplace for a long time.

stories.primary_headline: Those opposing electoral roll revision attempting to undermine democracy: Suresh Gopi

primary_source.headline: Those opposing electoral roll revision attempting to undermine democracy: Suresh Gopi
primary_source.content: Mangaluru: Those opposing Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls are attempting to undermine country’s democracy and electoral system, Union Minister of State for Petroleum and Natural Gas Suresh Gopi charged on Friday."Future generations will regard them as betrayers of trust and traitors to the nation," emphasised the actor Suresh Gopi. He was addressing gathering after inaugurating a public meeting organised as part of Bharatiya Janata Party’s ‘Save Democracy, End Anarchy campaign at Kadri ground. Suresh Gopi quoting a verse from renowned Tamil poet Subramania Bharathiyar's famous poem, ‘Bharata Samudayam Vazhgave; Vazhga Vazhga Bharata Samudayam Vazhgave’, declared that it was unfortunate that a ruling party had been compelled to organise a protest in response to an agitation organised by the opposition.He alleged that those spreading misinformation about the SIR, which is being undertaken to ensure the integrity of electoral politics, were misleading the country’s youth. Mangaluru: Union minister Suresh Gopi to take part in march against Congress over electoral rolls misinformation“Kharge’s son should understand that Narendra Modi is not going anywhere from this country. It is your leader and his family who should leave. If they do not go voluntarily, the people themselves will lift them up and throw them into the Arabian Sea,” Suresh Gopi declared.He added that the protest meeting was only the beginning and warned that the anger of the people would engulf all those opposing the initiative.BJP national spokesperson Gaurav Bhatia, BJP DK district president Satish Kumpala, Udupi district president Naveen Shetty Kuthyaru, Kasaragod district president N L Ashwini, MP Captain Brijesh Chowta, Kota Srinivas Poojary, MLAs D Vedavyas Kamath, Harish Poonja, Rajesh Naik Ulipadyguthu, K Umanath Kotian, Gurme Suresh Shetty, Bhagirathi Murulya, Gururaj Gantihole, Dr Y Bharath Shetty, Yashpal Suvarna, Kiran Kumar Kodgi, MLCs Kishore Kumar Puttur, Pratapsimha Nayak among olthers participated in the meeting.

stories.primary_headline: IMA urges CBFC to deny certification to Sunny Deol-starrer, says film glorifies violence against medics

primary_source.headline: IMA urges CBFC to deny certification to Sunny Deol-starrer, says film glorifies violence against medics
primary_source.content:
New Delhi: The Indian Medical Association (IMA) has urged the Central Board of Film Certification (CBFC) to refuse certification to the upcoming Hindi film Suryaa: Ant Se Aarambh Tak, alleging that its teaser glorifies violence against doctors.In a representation to the CBFC chairperson dated November 4, IMA national president Dr Anilkumar J Nayak said the film, starring Sunny Deol and Ravi Kishan, attributes corruption to doctors as a class and presents assaulting doctors and hospital personnel inside a hospital as a "justified and heroic act."Directed by M Padmakumar, the film is scheduled for a nationwide theatrical release on November 20. Its official teaser was released on YouTube on October 19.The IMA said the teaser contains dialogues alleging that doctors charge exorbitant amounts, conduct unnecessary tests and accept commissions instead of writing prescriptions."Doctors don't write prescriptions; they write their commissions," the lead character says in the teaser, according to the representation.It also objects to scenes showing the lead character physically assaulting doctors, nursing staff and hospital personnel inside a hospital, claiming that such acts are presented as heroic and justified."The Film is likely to incite the commission of offences against doctors and other healthcare professionals, is against the interests of public order, involves defamation of registered medical practitioners as a body, and glorifies and justifies violence against doctors," the representation said.The association cited incidents of attacks on healthcare professionals across the country, including the stabbing death of a 22-year-old intern, Dr Vandana Das, in Kerala in May 2023, the assault on a doctor at a hospital in Kozhikode in October 2025 and attacks on resident doctors in Aligarh and Mumbai this year.'Satluj' director Honey Trehan criticises new CBFC guidelines, calls them 'cowardness and dictatorship'
It also cited a survey of 1,566 healthcare workers by experts from VMMC and Safdarjung Hospital and AIIMS, reported in May 2026, which found that 58.2 per cent of them felt unsafe at their workplace and 78.4 per cent had faced threats while on duty.The IMA said assaults on doctors by patients, relatives and attendants are a recurring feature of Indian hospitals and that the potential of the film to incite violence must be assessed in the prevailing conditions.It argued that violence in hospitals affects the community at large as attacks can disrupt medical services, endanger patients awaiting treatment and create an atmosphere of fear among healthcare workers.The association said the film violates Section 5B of the Cinematograph Act, 1952, which prohibits certification of films that are against public order, involve defamation, or are likely to incite the commission of an offence.It also cited the revised Guidelines for Certification of Films for Public Exhibition issued on September 16, arguing that the film violates provisions prohibiting glorification or justification of violence, depiction of visuals likely to incite offences and content involving defamation of an individual or a body of individuals.The IMA said the film's "objectionable" content forms its core theme and cannot be removed through mere excisions.It requested the CBFC to exhibit the film before IMA representatives and allow a medical expert nominated by the association to view it along with the examining committee.The association also sought an opportunity to be heard before any certification decision is taken and urged the board to refer the film to a revising committee if the examining committee recommends certification.The IMA said the film had not been submitted to the CBFC for certification as of October 22, according to the Information and Broadcasting Ministry.
